From: Priya Singh <security@medixhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Narrowed subprocessor scope & temporary agent declaration — Medix Health

Hi Evelyn / team,

Quick one from Medix security as we ramp the pilot. We received your recent subprocessor roster but need two things before we can sign off on the sandbox pilot:

1) A narrowed scope statement for any temporary/onboarded subprocessors used for telemetry and log aggregation (we only want processing for telemetry metadata, no patient data).
2) Attestation from the telemetry vendor that they will run in a dedicated, encrypted bucket and will not persist raw request payloads beyond 24 hours (we asked EdgeFlux specifically).

Can you: (a) confirm which subprocessors will touch telemetry in the pilot, (b) provide an attestation from the vendor, and (c) mark any processors as "temporary" with an expected removal date?

We appreciate quick turnaround — pilot start target is 2028-06-10.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Senior InfoSec Manager, Medix Health
security@medixhealth.com

---
Note: attaching the snippet of the DPA clause we expect (see link below).

Subject: Re: Request: Narrowed subprocessor scope & temporary agent declaration — Medix Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Short answer: yes, we can provide the scope narrowing and vendor attestation for the pilot.

What I'm sending now:
- redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20280602.csv (attached) — annotated to show which subprocessors touch telemetry only and which may see customer payloads. Temporary status flags applied where appropriate.
- Requested: EdgeFlux attestation (we've asked them to produce a signed PDF; cc'd their ops contact).

Proposed temporary constraints for the pilot (summary):
- Telemetry-only processors: EdgeFlux (ingest), LogShelf (aggregator) — marked TEMP until 2028-07-15.
- No processor will receive raw PII or patient payloads; any identifying fields will be redacted at the request layer.
- Retention policy: temporary telemetry buckets retained <= 24 hours; aggregated metrics retained per Medix agreement.

Naomi / Kim / Jordan: please review the attached matrix and the bullet points above and confirm any legal/controls language we should use in the attestation. Once we have EdgeFlux's signed attestation I'll forward to Priya for their records.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Eve / team — quick legal notes inline. Forwarding to make edits visible to Priya after we confirm: 

On 2028-06-02 10:05, Evelyn Hart wrote: (see redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20280602.csv)

> Proposed temporary constraints for the pilot (summary):
> - Telemetry-only processors: EdgeFlux (ingest), LogShelf (aggregator) — marked TEMP until 2028-07-15.
> - No processor will receive raw PII or patient payloads; any identifying fields will be redacted at the request layer.
> - Retention policy: temporary telemetry buckets retained <= 24 hours; aggregated metrics retained per Medix agreement.

Legal edits (suggested):
- Replace "will not receive" with "are contractually prohibited from accessing or storing" for stronger enforceability.
- Add a required quarterly attestation clause for any temporary processor during the pilot (even if temporary).
- For the retention language, add an enforceable data purge requirement with verifiable logs (not just "per agreement").

Jordan: please confirm procurement impact if we add short-term procurement QA/attestations. Kim: verify we can technically enforce 24-hour auto-delete without retention lag in the pipeline.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Park <ops@edgeflux.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Narrowed subprocessor scope & temporary agent declaration — Medix Health

Hi Priya, Eve, team — Sean at EdgeFlux. Thanks for the heads-up; attaching our attestation PDF which covers all the bullets you requested. Short summary below and the signed attestation is attached (edgeflux_attestation_20280602.pdf).

Summary:
- Scope: EdgeFlux will only process telemetry metadata for the Medix pilot. No patient payloads will be stored or routed to EdgeFlux systems.
- Isolation: Telemetry will be written to a dedicated encrypted S3 bucket with server-side encryption (AES-256) and unique keys per customer.
- Retention: Raw telemetry logs are set to TTL=24 hours. Aggregates are pushed to Redshift for analytics (no raw payload).
- Access: Only EdgeFlux ops personnel named in the attestation have access; all access is logged and auditable.

We confirm the bucket will be provisioned in the US region and EdgeFlux will supply weekly deletion logs for the pilot period. If you need any additional wording for contract language, tell us and we'll update the PDF and re-sign.

Regards,
Sean Park
Head of Ops, EdgeFlux
ops@edgeflux.com
